question.prompt: If \(f(x)\) is a real-valued function of the real variable \(x,\) and \(f(x)\) is not identically zero, and for all \(a\) and \(b\) \[ \begin{gathered} f(a+b)+f(a-b)\\ =2f(a)+2f(b), \end{gathered} \] then for all \(x\) and \(y\)

solutions.explanation:
Because the identity holds for every pair of real inputs, we can use zero to simplify its arguments. First set \(a=b=0\). Then
\[
2f(0)=4f(0),
\]
so \(f(0)=0\).

Now set \(a=0\) and \(b=x\), where \(x\) is any real number. The given identity becomes
\[
f(x)+f(-x)=2f(0)+2f(x)=2f(x).
\]
Subtracting \(f(x)\) gives \(f(-x)=f(x)\). Thus \(f\) is even, and the answer is \(\boxed{\text{C}}\).
solutions.title: Use zero inputs
